Creating a prompt version no longer changes the tags dictionary you pass in. All 53 tests in `tests/entities/test_prompt.py` pass.

**The bug:** in `mlflow/entities/model_registry/prompt_version.py:214`, `PromptVersion.__init__` did `tags = tags or {}`. That kept a reference to your own dictionary, so the internal entries (template text, prompt type, prompt marker, model configuration) were written straight into it. The version then stored that same object as its own tags. So when you reused the dict, the second version inherited the first one's template and model configuration, which is why your "Hi!" version reported a temperature of 0.7.

**The fix:** I changed that line to `tags = dict(tags) if tags else {}`. Each version now works on its own shallow copy, your dictionary keeps exactly what you put in it, and nothing leaks between versions that share a tags dict. A shallow copy is enough because tag values are strings.

**Test:** `test_prompt_does_not_mutate_caller_tags` was already staged in `tests/entities/test_prompt.py`, and it matches your example. It checks that the caller's dict is still `{"author": "alice"}` after the first version is created. It also checks that a second version built from the same dict has `model_config is None` and only the user tags. I didn't change the test.
